from.place: Proof, second paragraph and conditions (a), (b): coherent sheaves are finite-coproduct preserving presheaves with equalizer descent along continuous surjections.

title: Coherent sheaf criterion on profinite sets
statement:
Fix a universe and let $\mathrm{Profinite}$ be the category of compact Hausdorff totally disconnected spaces and continuous maps. Its coherent topology is generated by the finite families $\{S_i\to S\}$ for which $\coprod_iS_i\to S$ is surjective. Let $\mathcal A$ be a category and $F:\mathrm{Profinite}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal A$ a presheaf. Then $F$ is a sheaf for this topology if and only if it takes finite disjoint coproducts, including the empty coproduct, to products [def-weil-category-product] and, for every continuous surjection $q:S'\to S$, the canonical diagram
$$F(S)\longrightarrow F(S')\rightrightarrows F(S'\times_S S')$$
is an equalizer in $\mathcal A$. Here $S'\times_S S'$ is the space of pairs $(x,y)$ with $q(x)=q(y)$, with its subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology]. In particular the criterion applies when $\mathcal A$ is the category of unital rings, without a commutativity assumption.
